a theoretical study of ReLU networks with a view towards the question of their redundancy.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the weight space of a ReLU network is parametrically equivalent to the set of functions it can implement, modulo permutations and scaling.
for any eligible architecture, any function implemented by some network can be implemented by some network that is obtained from the original network by applying only permutations and rescaling.
the parameterisation of a ReLU network is not redundant at all, and that all weight transformations are functionally relevant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show the existence of an isomorphism between the function spaces of ReLU networks and the space of all weight matrices.
ReLU networks are not redundant at all, and that the parameterisation of the weight space is in fact minimal.
ReLU networks with non-increasing width are not redundant in terms of their parameterisations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the parameterisation of a ReLU network can be significantly reduced without affecting its functionality.
the number of function-preserving transformations of a ReLU network is bounded by the product of its layer widths.

, in the context of ReLU networks with non-increasing width, the parameterisation is essentially unique, and thus the number of parameters in such networks can be considered as an intrinsic complexity measure.
